containers.about.fresh: A fresh snapshot: `POST /api/refresh` takes one at once and answers when it is written. Nothing takes one on a schedule.
containers.about.ports: «host network» means the container listens on the host itself, and Docker does not know its ports. The port behind DSM's reverse proxy is written beside the container: by the label arpa.home.lan.name in its compose, and in the host network also by its project's name. The table «Behind DSM's reverse proxy» lists every port behind the proxy.
containers.about.secrets: Only names, images, states, ports and the label arpa.home.lan.name are copied from Docker: no environment variables, no command lines, no mounts.
containers.idle.hint: Folders beside the map's with a compose file whose containers are all stopped, or were never created.

containers.stale: Stale: this snapshot is {age} old, three intervals and more. The watcher is not running: do not take this list as the present.

containers.taken-asked: Snapshot of {taken}, taken by the map's container watcher when asked: at its start and on `POST /api/refresh`. Docker {docker}, {os}.

gate.not-mounted: DSM on the NAS: its nginx folder is not mounted for the watcher, so the map does not know whom DSM lets through.
gate.not-read: DSM on the NAS: the watcher's snapshot holds no reading of DSM's gate; the watcher is older than this map.

llms.about: The structure of a local network, ready made: which networks exist, who lives in them and who may go where. The data is read from a home router, read-only.
llms.lang.about: Every address above takes `?lang=`, and English is what comes without it: {langs}. `/api/langs` lists them.
llms.lang.head: Language
llms.machine.containers: [/api/containers](/api/containers): the same list of containers and projects as JSON.
llms.machine.head: If a program is to read it
llms.machine.history: [/api/history](/api/history): the list of kept snapshots; any of them opens as `/network.md?at=<name>`.
llms.machine.houses: [/api/houses](/api/houses): who the network is talking to out in the world — every far end of the live walks, named by the router's own answers or by the map's table of services, and whatever nothing could name. The page for it is [/houses.html](/houses.html).
llms.machine.map: [/api/map](/api/map): the same snapshot as JSON, with every detail of the rules.
llms.machine.names: [/api/names](/api/names): the names the router answers itself — its static DNS records — grouped by the address they lead to, with whoever on the map holds it, and the DNS server each network's DHCP hands out. The page for it is [/names.html](/names.html).
llms.machine.openapi: [/openapi.json](/openapi.json): every route the map answers, as OpenAPI 3.1 — read off the server's own table, open without logging in.
llms.machine.packages: [/api/packages](/api/packages): what this copy of the map is made of — Python, its distributions and Alpine's packages, named as osv.dev names them; open without logging in.
llms.machine.specs: [/api/specs](/api/specs): the same as JSON — every device on the map with its key, addresses and card of characteristics, or `null` when nobody filled it in. To write a card: `PUT /api/specs`.
llms.mind.default-deny: Whatever is not in the access table is forbidden: between networks the default is deny.
llms.mind.doubts: The section on what could not be read matters: it lists where the real access may differ from the table.
llms.mind.gate: The router's table is not the last word on the NAS: DSM's reverse proxy may turn a network away from a name, or lead a name on past a road the router keeps shut. The section «The NAS's own gate» in /network.md says which.
llms.mind.head: Worth keeping in mind
llms.mind.snapshot: This is a snapshot, not a live network: the time it was taken is at the top of /network.md.
llms.no-clicking: There is no need to click the map: everything drawn on it is here as text.
llms.start.containers: [/containers.md](/containers.md): what runs on the map's host — every compose project there, its containers with image and tag, state and health, and what is present but not running. The snapshot is taken when asked, by `POST /api/refresh`; its time is at the top. It also names the next free port for a new app on that host.
llms.start.fresh: `POST /api/refresh` first, when the answer must be fresh: it takes the router's snapshot and the NAS's containers anew and answers only once both are written, within a minute. A snapshot younger than half a minute is not taken again. `curl -X POST <this map>/api/refresh`, then read.
llms.start.head: Start here
llms.start.specs: [/specs.md](/specs.md): what the owner's machines are made of — system and version, processor, physical and logical cores, RAM and its type, disks, graphics, role. When you need facts about the computers at home, read them here rather than asking the owner. To write one: `PUT /api/specs`, told at the end of /specs.md.
llms.start.story: [/network.md](/network.md): networks, devices and permissions in tables. One file, built afresh on every request.

specs.about: What the machines at home are made of: system, processor, cores, memory, disks. The owner and agents wrote it down: the router does not know it, and the map does not guess. The same as JSON: [/api/specs](/api/specs). The page for people: [/specs.html](/specs.html).
specs.field.role: role: what the machine is for
specs.hint: An empty field wipes its line. Agents write here too, with PUT /api/specs: how is told in /specs.md.
specs.how.about: `PUT /api/specs` with JSON and the headers `Content-Type: application/json` and `Origin: <this map>`. From a network that may move things on the map, any device's card. From another network the map is shown to, only the card of the device the request comes from: an agent writing down the machine it runs on. The fields:
specs.how.by: who wrote it: a person's or an agent's name.
specs.how.device: the device's key from /api/specs: a MAC or an address. Required.
specs.how.example: For example: `curl -X PUT <this map>/api/specs -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Origin: <this map>' -d '{"device": "<key>", "os": "Ubuntu", "os_version": "24.04", "cores": 8, "threads": 16, "ram_gb": 32, "by": "<who you are>"}'`
specs.how.name: the name on the map. It changes the map's own name too, and only from a network that may move things.
specs.how.wipe: An empty value wipes a line. Fields the request leaves out stay as they are. The answer is the device's card, as in /api/specs.
